weather_report:
Wembley settles into a wet hush tonight, the sort of late hour when the streets glow with reflected lamplight and umbrellas drip in doorways. Light rain earlier this evening lingered and may come and go in stray showers, leaving the air cool and faintly metallic. The sky is low and smudged, so clarity is soft rather than sharp; stars are off-stage. There’s no sunshine to speak of now, and the UV index is essentially nil; even by day it stayed muted beneath a stubborn lid of cloud.

It’s a gently unpleasant night only in the way dampness sneaks into cuffs and collars, so a light waterproof with a hood and shoes that can take a splash are your allies. If you’re stepping out, move unhurriedly and give the pavements their slick respect; if you’re staying in, it’s a good time to tidy tomorrow’s bag, let a kettle whisper, or take a brief umbrella walk around the block to air the mind. Expect the mood to remain subdued into the small hours, with the world feeling close, reflective, and a touch wistful.
